problem: Existing VLAs are mostly Markovian and confined to short-horizon table-top manipulation, lacking structured spatial and task-progress memory for mobile manipulation that couples navigation and manipulation. Prior memory-augmented methods use only an implicit perceptual cache (MemoryVLA) or LLM-side landmark maps (BSC-Nav).
motivation: Mobile manipulation is non-Markovian: visually similar frames can correspond to different task progress (e.g. cabinet opened vs. about to open), and the agent must remember scene layout across changing spatial contexts. The paper draws on the human declarative memory system (parahippocampal spatial/semantic memory plus hippocampal episodic memory) to design complementary memories. Large-scale mobile-manipulation data is also scarce, so the authors build an automated data engine.
key_idea: Equip a VLA with a synergistic declarative memory, a persistent voxel scene memory and a time-indexed episodic token buffer, retrieved via coarse and fine cross-attention to condition per-part (base/arm) diffusion policies.
insight: Both memories and both observation modalities matter: on PnP Counter-to-Stove, removing scene memory drops SR to 0.09 (mobile) / 0.16 (static) and removing episodic memory to 0.14 / 0.13, versus 0.17 / 0.21 for the full model. Removing RGB is the most damaging for the mobile variant (0.02). The window size (L=8) and update threshold (tau=0.5) matter; too short a window causes plan forgetting and too high a threshold leaves stale scene memory. Real-world analysis notes that episodic memory can compensate for scene-memory 'ghosting', but explicit 3D memory hurts under dynamic occlusion (fridge door).
method: Multimodal state tokens: frozen SigLIP text and vision towers (3 fixed cameras), trainable PointAttn encoder on fused depth point clouds, and an MLP for proprioception, concatenated into S_t = [L, V_t, P_t, R_t].

Scene memory: key-value voxel bank (keys are xyz, values are PointAttn features), initialized empty. Updated by EMA (alpha=0.2) only where the MLP-decoder reconstruction error exceeds tau=0.5; top-k entries in the current camera frustum are retrieved.
Episodic memory: FIFO buffer of the last k raw encoded token sequences S_t with timestamps (window L=8 optimal), uncompressed to keep detailed temporal cues.

Memory matching and attention: cosine-similarity top-k selection, then coarse cross-attention (query V3D_t over scene memory) and fine cross-attention (query S_t over episodic memory); outputs are concatenated into H_t.
Per-part diffusion policy: independent denoisers for base and arm conditioned on H_t, trained with a summed denoising loss.

MoMani data engine: MLLM-prompted online candidate generation (target-aligned sampling, safe navigation, nav-manip stitching) with hard quality gates, then offline lexicographic ranking and audit; produces 5,000+ trajectories (7,889 sim episodes), plus 1,200 real teleoperated episodes on TidyBot++.

setting.backbone: Frozen SigLIP encoders + trainable PointAttn + memory cross-attention + per-part diffusion policy (trained from scratch on top of frozen SigLIP)
setting.training_data: MoMani: 7,889 simulated RoboCasa episodes (57% navigation-only, 4 mobile manipulation tasks) and 1,200 real-robot teleoperated episodes on TidyBot++; trained on 8 A100 GPUs
setting.observation: multi-view (3 fixed cameras) RGB-D, point clouds, proprioception, language instruction
setting.action_space: continuous arm and holonomic base actions via per-part diffusion
setting.privileged: none stated (needs accurate depth and pose/odometry streams)

numbers.extra: SR averaged over 3 seeds, 50 episodes per task; trained on MoMani sim data

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark; results are on RoboCasa-based MoMani sim tasks and real-world tasks. Ablations (Table 2) on PnP Counter-to-Stove and sensitivity (Table 3) not listed as separate entries.
results: In RoboCasa simulation EchoVLA reaches average SR 0.52 on manipulation/navigation and 0.31 on mobile manipulation, beating pi0.5 (0.32 and 0.20) by +0.20 and +0.11. In real-world TidyBot++ tests it gets 0.44 mean SR versus pi0.5 0.33 and Diffusion Policy 0.32, though it underperforms on OR (0.40 vs 0.50 for pi0.5) and OD/PCIS margins are small.
limitations: Relies on high-quality depth and pose; odometry drift causes ghosting in scene memory.
Explicit 3D scene memory degrades under dynamic occlusion (e.g. fridge door opening) and suffers cold start in novel environments.
Absolute success rates remain low (0.31 sim mobile manipulation; 0.10 on the long-horizon real EnP task) and evaluation is limited to a few tasks in kitchen scenes.
